mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a risk premium adjustment that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05) during inflation spikes above 0.3%, or the S&P 500 declines despite the CPIAUCSL spike.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index exceeding 0.5% is associated with higher wage growth expectations, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative even when PAYEMS rises >0.5%, or the effect is not significant after controlling for GDP growth (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in INDPRO supply index below 100 signals weak manufacturing momentum, which tends to precede negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains below 100 for at least 3 consecutive months without a subsequent negative 5-day SPX return.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both HOUST and RSAFS retail and business demand indices by at least 2% in the same month predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: both HOUST and RSAFS fall by ≥2% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the simultaneous demand drop, or the interaction is not statistically significant (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 4%, the increased discount rate erodes equity present value, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS > 4%, or the effect is not robust across multiple policy rate shocks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 3.8% for three consecutive months is a leading indicator of tighter labor markets, which tends to drive positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when UNRATE remains above 3.8% for 3 months, or the effect is not significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in GDPC1 demand index (≥5% month-over-month) coincides with investor caution and is associated with negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by ≥5% from previous month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive despite the GDPC1 decline, or the shock is not statistically significant (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (each by ≥0.2% in the same month) signal dual disinflation, which tends to produce positive 20-day S&P 500 returns in a recovery regime.
candidate_trigger: both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL fall by ≥0.2% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the dual decline, or the interaction is not statistically significant (F-test p > 0.05).
